mike: hey team, follow-up on the nsys run I dropped in #artifacts — seeing periodic cudaMalloc spikes that align with KV cache misses.
anya: can you paste the timeline view? quick screenshot would help.
mike: pasted below — you'll see a ~5-8ms gap every ~120ms where there are big host allocations, then kernels stall. looks like allocation contention.
mike: ```
# nsys timeline snippet
Time(ms)  Kernel      PID   GPU(s)  Activity
120.34    cudaMalloc  4321  0       7.9ms
128.54    cudnnGEMM   4321  0       2.3ms
240.78    cudaMalloc  4321  0       8.1ms
249.05    attention_k 4321  0       1.8ms
```
raj: interesting — are those mallocs coming from the runtime allocator or from an external library?
chloe: we log cublas/cuDNN allocations — those are fine. my bet is the KV cache allocation path: we reallocate shards when prefix growth triggers new pages.
mike: I grep'd traces — callstack shows our kv_cache::ensure_capacity -> cudaMalloc.
anya: that explains periodic nature: requests with long contexts trigger re-reserve. batching might be hitting mixed-length requests so cache growth happens mid-batch.
perf-bot: regression detected: 2026-02-28 deployment -> avg p95 latency +12% on chat workloads. correlated with commit 9f4b3 that changed arena resizing.
raj: commit 9f4b3 replaced fixed arenas with on-demand expand using cudaMalloc/free to reduce upfront memory. that saved peak mem but probably added fragmentation/latency.
chloe: quick mitigation: switch to cudarMallocAsync + cudaMemPool or pre-reserve a dedicated pool for KV cache shards. cudarMallocAsync reduces host syncs.
mike: I ran a small experiment: enabling cudarMallocAsync + single-threaded pool for KV cuts the malloc stall events almost entirely in local nsys traces. p95 dropped by ~7%.
anya: did you try tuning pool thresholds? fragmentation can still bite if shard sizes vary a lot.
mike: yes — I added an arena bucket strategy: small (<=64KB), med (64KB-4MB), large (>4MB). allocate from corresponding subpool. code diff in sandbox: ```cpp
// pseudo
if (size <= 64k) alloc_from(small_pool);
else if (size <= 4M) alloc_from(med_pool);
else alloc_via_async(size);
```
raj: sounds good. also consider reusing freed KV buffers immediately into same pool instead of returning to driver — reduces churn.
chloe: one weird thing: even with pools, nsys shows occasional host-side memcpy stalls. could be that pooling reduces allocations but increases memcpy to zero newly allocated pages. we should use cuMemAdvise/CUDA_MEMCPY_ASYNC or use cudaMemsetAsync after allocation on stream.
anya: another angle: batching heuristics. if we reorder requests by sequence length within a small time window (micro-batching sorter) we can avoid mid-batch growth. that reduces number of times we need to expand cache during an active batch.
mike: tested length-bucketed batching with 50ms coalescing window — reduces allocation events by ~30% and improves throughput for mixed workloads. tradeoff: slight added latency for small fraction of requests.
raj: for long-term: implement a background growing thread that expands arenas off the critical path. allow a request to signal required capacity; background thread performs cudaMallocAsync and links pages when ready.
chloe: agree. also add eviction compaction: when we evict old KV pages, try to coalesce adjacent free segments before returning to driver. reduces fragmentation.
mike: action items: (1) prototype cudaMallocAsync + mempool + bucketed arenas (2) add micro-batcher by length to reduce on-path growth (3) instrument nsys tracepoints around kv_allocator alloc/free and arena hits/misses so we can quantify.
anya: I can pick up (2). mike take (1), raj you own (3) instrumentation and dashboards. i'll create a lightweight perf test that mixes short/long contexts.
raj: I'll add tracepoints and push a small perf dashboard: KV alloc rate, pool hit ratio, malloc/free host stalls, p95 latency.
chloe: once we have traces, we should run perfetto on a long soak to catch low-rate fragmentation events. nsys captures are good for kernel timelines but perfetto gives system-wide view incl. CPU allocation threads.
perf-bot: noted. tagging regression ticket INF-786.
mike: thanks — I'll share the sandbox PR + nsys captures in the thread in a bit. :thumbsup:
anya: sounds good. small follow-up: add a flag to force eager pre-reserve for enterprise customers who prefer latency vs memory tradeoffs.
chloe: yep, config flag makes sense.
raj: cool. locking this thread for now — will post dashboards when ready.
